title: Feds ‘should run as fast as' they can from Alto project, say opposition MPs, as PBO estimates construction alone could cost $113-billion — The Hill Times

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Feds ‘should run as fast as' they can from Alto project, say opposition MPs, as PBO estimates construction alone could cost $113-billion  - The Hill Times

'There is no remotely believable scenario under which Alto will break even. So, the best thing to do is to stop spending taxpayer dollars on it,' says Conservative MP Scott Reid.

Actual Article Body:
The federal government should “re-evaluate” the Alto high-speed rail project and instead consider improving the VIA Rail, say opposition MPs, as Canada’s budget watchdog warns good project management will be “essential” to avoid cost overruns after a recent report found the build alone could cost up to $113-billion—roughly 25 per cent more than the government’s initial calculations.

Parliamentary Budget Officer (PBO) Annette Ryan’s Oct. 1 analysis on the construction cost of the government’s planned Alto high-speed rail project (HSR) revealed that the project’s Toronto-Quebec City corridor could cost between $75-billion and $113-billion, a higher range than the government’s initial $60-billion to $90-billion forecast.

Actual Article Body:
Sochi bloggers Svetlana Izhilenko and Alisa Kunyashova said they were fired from a local Pyaterochka grocery store after posting a video about rising grocery prices the day after the elections.

On September 21, Izhilenko and Kunyashova, who worked at the store, posted a reel about changing grocery price tags. “We’ve been changing price tags all morning, and we’re in shock. The elections are over, and now almost all the groceries cost 20–30 rubles more,” Izhilenko said in the video, without naming the store. The video drew 5.7 million views and 180,000 likes.
